Calculate the final pressure after the given duration by applying the pressurization or depressurization rate, stopping exactly at the target if reached, and never exceeding the safe caps. Return a list of final pressures. Example input: [(80, 100, 10), (100, 20, 5)]. Example output: [100, 60].

title: Music Festival Scheduler
spec: Determine performance times for a festival stage. The entry function `schedule(bands)` processes a list of tuples containing band genre, requested duration, and popularity score. The standard set time is forty five minutes. The changeover gap between bands is fifteen minutes. The curfew time is one thousand minutes from the festival start. A popularity score over eighty grants a headline set time of ninety minutes instead of the standard time (unless the requested duration is shorter). Return a list of tuples representing the start and end times in minutes from zero for each band, scheduled sequentially. Example input: [("rock", 60, 50), ("pop", 120, 85)]. Example output: [(0, 45), (60, 150)].

title: Food Truck Profitability
spec: Evaluate the daily financial performance of a food truck. The entry function `profit(days)` accepts a list of tuples containing meals sold, ingredients cost, and hours parked. The sale price per meal is twelve. The daily permit fee is thirty. The hourly parking rate is five. The spoilage rate is ten percent of the ingredients cost, added as an extra expense. The minimum profit target is one hundred. Return a list of tuples containing the net profit and a boolean indicating if the target was met. Example input: [(50, 100, 4), (10, 50, 2)]. Example output: [(440.0, True), (25.0, False)].

title: Internet Cafe Billing
spec: Calculate session charges for users at an internet cafe. The entry function `charge(sessions)` takes a list of tuples containing minutes used, a boolean for premium tier, and pages printed. The hourly base rate is four. The premium hourly rate is seven. Printing costs twenty cents per page. The minimum charge is equivalent to one hour, even for shorter sessions. A late night discount of twenty percent applies to the entire bill if the session duration exceeds one hundred eighty minutes. Return a list of the final prices for each session. Example input: [(30, False, 5), (240, True, 0)]. Example output: [5.0, 22.4].

title: Bus Fleet Maintenance
spec: Assess maintenance needs and costs for a fleet of buses. The entry function `inspect(buses)` receives a list of tuples with total mileage, days since last service, and incident count. The oil change interval is five thousand miles. The major inspection threshold is fifty thousand miles. The tire lifespan is thirty thousand miles. The base service cost is two hundred. Each service type due adds to the base cost: oil changes add fifty, tires add four hundred, major inspections add one thousand. An incident penalty adds fifty per incident. A service is due if the mileage is cleanly divisible by its respective threshold. Return a list of total costs for each bus. Example input: [(15000, 100, 1), (50000, 200, 0)]. Example output: [300, 1250].

title: Bakery Production Planner
spec: Schedule baking times and calculate revenue for bread orders. The entry function `plan(orders)` accepts a list of tuples containing loaf count, string for bread type, and a boolean for urgent priority. The oven maximum capacity is twenty loaves at a time. Standard baking time is forty minutes per batch. Sourdough requires an additional resting time of one hundred twenty minutes before baking. The urgent fee adds fifteen to the order revenue. The base cost per loaf is three. Return a list of tuples with total time in minutes to complete all batches and total revenue for each order. Example input: [(30, "white", False), (10, "sourdough", True)]. Example output: [(80, 90), (160, 45)].

title: Carnival Game Payouts
spec: Compute the number of reward tickets for carnival game plays. The entry function `payout(games)` processes a list of tuples with score, string for game type, and a boolean for VIP status. The base conversion rate is one ticket per ten points. The jackpot limit caps payouts at five hundred tickets per game. VIP members receive a bonus of twenty percent extra tickets. The minimum payout for participating is five tickets. Premium games apply a multiplier of two to the points before ticket conversion. Return a list of integer tickets awarded. Example input: [(30, "standard", False), (3000, "premium", True)]. Example output: [5, 500].

title: Mining Excavation Planner
spec: Estimate depths and costs for mining sites. The entry function `excavate(sites)` accepts a list of tuples with depth to clear, rock hardness scale from one to ten, and hours allocated. The standard digging rate is ten meters per hour. A hardness scale of seven or above triggers a hard rock penalty, slowing the digging rate by forty percent. The maximum daily operation limit is twelve hours; allocated hours are capped at this limit. A blast bonus adds five meters for free at the start of any site requesting more than fifty meters of clearance. The base cost per hour is one hundred. Return a list of tuples with actual depths reached and total cost for each site based on the hours used. Example input: [(100, 5, 10), (40, 8, 15)]. Example output: [(105, 1000), (72, 1200)].

title: Aerial Mapping Battery Estimator
spec: Calculate battery requirements for drone mapping flights. The entry function `survey(regions)` receives a list of tuples representing square meters, wind speed, and a boolean for high resolution. The standard coverage rate is one hundred square meters per minute. High resolution mapping cuts the coverage speed by half. The maximum battery flight time is thirty minutes. A wind speed over fifteen reduces total battery life by five minutes due to resistance. The safe return margin reserves five minutes of each battery. Return a list of the integer number of batteries needed to complete each region, rounding up to the next whole battery. Example input: [(2000, 10, False), (2500, 20, True)]. Example output: [1, 3].

title: Cruise Ship Provisioning
spec: Determine food and water supplies for cruise voyages. The entry function `provision(voyages)` accepts a list of tuples with passenger count, duration in days, and a boolean for luxury tier. The standard meals per passenger day is three. The water daily ration per person is five liters. The buffer percentage is fifteen percent extra for all calculated supplies. The crew ratio requires one crew member for every four passengers, and crew members consume the same base rations. Luxury voyages add two liters of water per person (passengers and crew) daily. Return a list of tuples with total meals and water volume needed, factoring in the buffer percentage. Example input: [(400, 5, False)]. Example output: [(8625.0, 14375.0)].

title: Ice Cream Parlor Stocker
spec: Estimate inventory requirements based on customer forecasts. The entry function `stock(forecasts)` takes a list of tuples containing expected customer count, a boolean for hot weather, and a boolean for the weekend. The average scoops per customer is two. There are fifty scoops per tub. The hot weather multiplier increases total expected scoops by one and a half. The weekend multiplier increases total expected scoops by one and a quarter. The absolute minimum safety stock is two tubs, added to the final order regardless of multipliers. Return a list of the integer number of tubs to order, rounding up before adding the safety stock. Example input: [(100, False, False), (200, True, True)]. Example output: [6, 17].

title: Rollercoaster Safety Analyzer
spec: Analyze the physical forces experienced on track segments. The entry function `analyze(segments)` processes a list of tuples with velocity in meters per second, track radius in meters, and a boolean for whether it is a loop. The gravity standard is nine point eight. The safe force limit is four point five Gs. The minimum velocity for a loop is fifteen. The loop multiplier increases effective force by one point two. Calculate the base force as velocity squared divided by the product of radius and gravity standard. If it is a loop, multiply the calculated force by the loop multiplier. Return a list of strings: warning if over the safe limit, invalid if a loop is too slow, or safe otherwise. Example input: [(20, 10, False), (10, 15, True)]. Example output: ["safe", "invalid"].

title: Subway Fare Collector
spec: Calculate passenger fares for a rapid transit network. The entry function `collect(trips)` takes a list of tuples with zones crossed, a boolean for peak hour, and a boolean for senior citizen. The zone base fare is two. The extra zone cost is one per zone crossed beyond the first. The peak surcharge adds one and a half to the final fare. The senior discount reduces the base fare and extra zone costs by fifty percent before any surcharges. The absolute maximum fare cap is seven. Return a list of the final calculated fare for each trip. Example input: [(1, False, False), (5, True, True)]. Example output: [2.0, 4.5].

title: Fish Farm Feeder
spec: Compute daily feed amounts for aquaculture tanks. The entry function `feed(tanks)` receives a list of tuples containing fish count, average weight in grams, and water temperature. The base daily pellet ratio is two percent of total biomass. The optimal temperature is twenty. A cold weather penalty applies if the temperature drops below fifteen, reducing feeding by thirty percent. An oxygen threshold multiplier increases feed by twenty percent if the temperature is exactly optimal. The maximum feed per tank is five thousand grams. Return a list of the daily feed amount for each tank. Example input: [(1000, 50, 20), (500, 100, 10)]. Example output: [1200.0, 700.0].

title: Lumber Mill Sorter
spec: Evaluate raw logs to predict lumber yields. The entry function `sort(logs)` accepts a list of tuples with log length, log diameter, and a defect count. The standard board length is eight. The minimum usable diameter is ten; logs below this yield zero boards and are labeled scrap. The premium defect tolerance is zero. The standard defect tolerance is three. The production waste factor discards twenty percent of the log length before cutting. Calculate the integer number of full standard length boards from the usable length. Categorize the total boards as premium if defects meet the premium tolerance, standard if within standard tolerance, or scrap if higher. Return a list of tuples with category string and board count. Example input: [(50, 12, 0), (30, 8, 1)]. Example output: [("premium", 5), ("scrap", 0)].

title: Rideshare Earnings Calculator
spec: Compute driver payouts for completed rides. The entry function `earnings(rides)` takes a list of tuples containing distance in miles, wait time in minutes, and a boolean for surge pricing. The base fare is three. The per mile rate is one point five. The wait minute rate is zero point twenty five. The platform fee takes twenty percent of the gross fare. The surge multiplier increases the gross fare by fifty percent before the platform fee is applied. Return a list of net earnings for each ride. Example input: [(10, 5, False), (4, 10, True)]. Example output: [15.4, 13.8].

title: Snowplow Routing Assessor
spec: Calculate operational time and material usage for snow clearing routes. The entry function `assess(routes)` processes a list of tuples with snow depth, road length, and a boolean for residential zones. The base blade clearing speed is twenty. The heavy snow threshold is six; depths above this apply a slowdown factor of fifty percent to the current speed. The residential speed limit caps the maximum speed at fifteen. The salt spread rate is two per unit of road length. Return a list of tuples containing time taken and salt used for each route. Example input: [(4, 100, False), (8, 60, True)]. Example output: [(5.0, 200), (6.0, 120)].

title: Archery Tournament Scorer
spec: Tabulate scores from archery target hits. The entry function `score(arrows)` receives a list of tuples with distance from center, wind speed, and time taken to shoot in seconds. The bullseye radius is two. The inner ring radius is five. The outer ring radius is ten. Bullseye hits award ten points. Inner hits award seven points. Outer hits award three points. Anything further is zero. A time penalty triggers if the time taken exceeds twenty seconds, deducting one point from that arrow. Wind speeds over fifteen invalidate the time penalty. Return a tuple containing the total score of all arrows and a count of bullseyes. Example input: [(1, 10, 25), (6, 20, 30)]. Example output: (12, 1).

title: Network Packet Validator
spec: Write a function called `filter(packets)` that cleans incoming network data. The input is a list of tuples containing four numbers: protocol version, header size in bytes, payload size in bytes, and time to live. The minimum valid header size is twenty. The maximum allowed payload size is fifteen hundred. The expected protocol version is four. For each packet, discard it if the protocol version is incorrect, the header is too small, or the payload is too large. If the time to live is zero or less, discard it as well. For valid packets, decrease the time to live by one and include them in the returned list. For example, given [(4, 24, 500, 10), (5, 20, 100, 5), (4, 15, 200, 8)], the output should be [(4, 24, 500, 9)].

title: Chess Material Evaluator
spec: Write a function `evaluate(pieces)` that determines the material advantage in a standard board position. The input is a list of tuples containing the player color and the piece type as strings. The piece values are: pawns are worth one point, knights are three points, bishops are three points, rooks are five points, and queens are nine points. Kings are not scored. Calculate the total score for white and the total score for black. Return the difference as a single number, representing white's total score minus black's total score. For example, given [("white", "knight"), ("white", "pawn"), ("black", "rook")], the score is four for white and five for black, yielding an output of -1.

title: Earthquake Severity Categorizer
spec: Write a function `categorize(magnitudes)` that processes a list of seismic readings. The minor threshold is four point zero. The moderate threshold is five point five. The severe threshold is seven point zero. The catastrophic threshold is eight point zero. Any reading below the minor threshold is considered micro. Return a tuple containing five counts: the number of micro, minor, moderate, severe, and catastrophic earthquakes in the provided list. Readings exactly on a threshold belong to the higher category. For example, given [3.2, 4.0, 6.1, 8.5], the output should be (1, 1, 1, 0, 1).

title: Fabric Loom Consumption
spec: Write a function `calculate(patterns)` to determine the total yarn required for weaving. The input is a list of tuples representing the width and length of each fabric piece in inches. The warp tension multiplier is one point zero five. The weft overlap allowance is two inches per row. The breakage loss factor is zero point zero five. The standard thread density is forty threads per inch. For each piece, calculate the warp length as length times tension multiplier times width times thread density. Calculate the weft length as width plus overlap allowance, times length times thread density. Add both, apply the breakage loss factor by multiplying the sum by one point zero five, and return the grand total across all patterns. For example, given [(10, 20)], the output should be 26040.0.

title: Hurricane Wind Categorizer
spec: Write a function `classify(speeds)` that evaluates maximum sustained wind speeds in knots. The minimum speed for category one is sixty four. Category two starts at eighty three. Category three starts at ninety six. Category four starts at one hundred thirteen. Category five begins at one hundred thirty seven. Speeds below category one are classified as tropical storms. Evaluate the list of integer wind speeds and return a list of corresponding string labels ranging from "storm" to "five". For example, given [50, 90, 140], the output should be ["storm", "two", "five"].

title: Steel Tempering Validator
spec: Write a function `validate(profiles)` that checks industrial heating cycles for safety. The input is a list of tuples containing the maximum temperature reached, the soak time in minutes, and the cooling rate in degrees per minute. The critical heating temperature minimum is seven hundred twenty. The minimum required soak time is forty five minutes. The maximum allowed cooling rate is fifty degrees per minute. Return a list of booleans indicating whether each heating profile meets all three structural criteria. For example, given [(750, 50, 40), (700, 60, 30)], the output should be [True, False].

title: Sourdough Starter Tracker
spec: Write a function `simulate(days)` that calculates the weight of a culture over time. The starting weight is always one hundred grams. The daily discard percentage is fifty percent. The feeding addition equals the weight remaining after the discard. The daily ambient growth multiplier is one point two. For each day, subtract the discard amount, add the feeding amount, and then multiply the total by the ambient growth multiplier. Return the final weight as a float rounded to two decimal places. For example, given 2 days, the sequence goes from 100 to 120.0, then to 144.0, so the output is 144.0.

title: Timber Yield Estimator
spec: Write a function `estimate(logs)` that calculates the usable wood volume from a harvest. The input is a list of tuples containing the log length in feet and the base diameter in inches. The bark thickness deduction is ten percent of the base diameter. The taper reduction factor is zero point two inches of diameter lost per foot of length. The minimum usable tip diameter is six inches. For each log, calculate the tip diameter by subtracting both the bark deduction and the taper reduction times length from the base diameter. If the tip diameter is below the minimum, the log is rejected and yields zero. Otherwise, add the log length to the total usable length. Return the total usable length across all logs. For example, given [(20, 14), (10, 8)], the output should be 20.

title: Book Binding Margin Calculator
spec: Write a function `spine(books)` that determines cover dimensions for printing. The input is a list of page counts. The thickness per page is zero point zero five millimeters. The bleed margin is three millimeters. The cover fold allowance is fifteen millimeters. The minimum physical spine width is five millimeters. Calculate the required spine width for each book based on the page count. If the calculated spine is less than the minimum physical spine, use the minimum instead. The total cover width is three hundred plus the spine width, plus twice the bleed margin, plus twice the fold allowance. Return a list of total cover widths. For example, given [50, 200], the output should be [341.0, 346.0].

title: Medication Dosage Checker
spec: Write a function `verify(requests)` that ensures prescription safety. The input is a list of tuples containing patient weight in kilograms, requested single dose in milligrams, and the daily total administered so far. The maximum safe single dose is five hundred. The maximum safe daily total is two thousand. The weight safety limit is ten milligrams per kilogram for a single dose. Check each request against these three limits. If the single dose exceeds the max single dose, the single dose exceeds the weight limit, or the single dose plus the daily total exceeds the daily max, reject it. Return a list of booleans representing approval. For example, given [(60, 400, 1500), (40, 450, 0)], the output should be [True, False].

title: Exam Curve Adjuster
spec: Write a function `curve(scores)` that normalizes a class grading distribution. The target class average is eighty five. The absolute maximum score is one hundred. The baseline minimum boost is two points. Calculate the average of the provided list of scores. Find the difference between the target average and the actual average. If this difference is less than the baseline minimum boost, use the minimum boost instead. Add this final boost value to every score in the list. Cap any resulting score at the absolute maximum score. Return the list of adjusted scores rounded to the nearest whole number. For example, given [80, 90, 88], the average is 86, which is higher than the target, so apply the baseline boost of 2, resulting in [82, 92, 90].

title: Supermarket Checkout Simulator
spec: Write a function `simulate(carts)` that estimates queuing times. The input is a list of integers representing the number of items in each customer's cart. The scan time per item is two seconds. The payment processing overhead is thirty seconds per customer. The maximum item limit for the express lane is fifteen. Distribute the carts sequentially: any cart with the express limit or fewer goes to the express lane, and all others go to the regular lane. Return a tuple containing the total processing time in seconds for the express lane and the total processing time for the regular lane. For example, given [5, 20, 10], the output should be (100, 70).

title: Soil Amendment Calculator
spec: Write a function `amend(readings)` that prescribes agricultural corrections. The input is a list of current soil pH readings. The target ideal level is six point five. The lime application factor is two hundred pounds per full unit of deficit. The sulfur application factor is fifty pounds per full unit of excess. For each reading, if it is below the target, calculate the deficit and multiply by the lime factor. If it is above the target, calculate the excess and multiply by the sulfur factor. Return a list of adjustments rounded to one decimal place, using positive numbers for lime additions and negative numbers for sulfur additions. For example, given [6.0, 7.5, 6.5], the output should be [100.0, -50.0, 0.0].

title: Ferry Loading Balancer
spec: Write a function `load(queue)` that determines boarding capacity. The input is a list of tuples containing the passenger type as a string and their respective group size or vehicle weight. The vehicle deck capacity is forty vehicles. The passenger deck capacity is two hundred people. The total safe weight limit is seventy five thousand pounds. An average walk-on passenger is estimated at one hundred fifty pounds. Iterate through the queue. If it is a vehicle, check if adding its weight exceeds the safe weight limit or if the vehicle deck is full. If it is a walk-on group, check if the passenger count exceeds the passenger deck capacity or the weight limit. Stop boarding as soon as any limit prevents the next item from boarding. Return the number of vehicles and the number of walk-on individuals that successfully boarded. For example, given [("vehicle", 4000), ("walk-on", 5)], the output should be (1, 5).

title: Landfill Capacity Forecaster
spec: Write a function `forecast(deliveries)` that projects waste site longevity. The input is a list of daily incoming trash volumes in cubic meters. The mechanical compaction rate is zero point six, meaning trash is compressed to sixty percent of its original volume. The daily soil cover requirement is fifty cubic meters, added at the end of each day. The maximum site volume limit is one hundred thousand cubic meters. Keep a running total of the consumed volume. For each day, add the compacted trash volume and the daily soil cover to the total. Return the day index (starting from zero) when the total volume strictly exceeds the maximum limit, or negative one if the limit is never exceeded. For example, given [50000, 80000, 20000], the output should be 1.

title: Aircraft Weight Balancer
spec: Write a function `balance(manifest)` that checks flight loading restrictions. The input is a list of tuples containing cargo weight in pounds and its position in inches from the datum line. The maximum gross weight is ten thousand pounds. The forward center of gravity limit is two hundred inches. The aft center of gravity limit is three hundred fifty inches. Calculate the total weight and the total moment by multiplying each weight by its position and summing them. Determine the center of gravity by dividing the total moment by the total weight. Return true if the total weight is less than or equal to the maximum and the center of gravity falls inclusively between the forward and aft limits, otherwise false. For example, given [(5000, 250), (2000, 300)], the output should be True.

title: Gear Train Efficiency
spec: Write a function `efficiency(gears)` that evaluates mechanical transmission limits. The input is a list of teeth counts for a sequence of meshed gears. The minimum allowed teeth count is twelve. The maximum allowed teeth count is one hundred twenty. The friction loss per meshing stage is zero point zero three. The base theoretical efficiency is one point zero. First, check if any gear falls outside the minimum or maximum allowed teeth; if so, return zero. The number of meshing stages is the number of gears minus one. Calculate the overall efficiency by subtracting the total friction loss (stages multiplied by friction loss per stage) from the base efficiency. Return the final efficiency rounded to two decimal places. For example, given [20, 40, 60], the output should be 0.94.

title: River Flood Warning System
spec: Write a function `monitor(levels)` that triggers emergency alerts. The input is a list of hourly water height readings in feet. The minor flood threshold is twelve feet. The moderate flood threshold is fifteen feet. The major flood threshold is twenty feet. Iterate through the readings and track the highest danger level reached. Return a single string indicating the peak condition: "major" if the major threshold is met or exceeded, "moderate" if the moderate threshold is reached, "minor" if the minor threshold is reached, or "normal" if all readings stay below the minor threshold. For example, given [10.5, 12.2, 14.8, 11.0], the output should be "minor".

title: Staircase Safety Validator
spec: Write a function `inspect(stairs)` that checks building code compliance. The input is a list of tuples representing individual step measurements: riser height and tread depth in inches. The maximum allowed riser height is seven point seven five. The minimum allowed tread depth is ten. The maximum allowed variance between the tallest and shortest riser in the entire staircase is zero point three seven five. Iterate through the steps and ensure every riser and tread meets the individual limits. Finally, check the overall variance across all risers. Return true if all individual and variance constraints are satisfied, otherwise false. For example, given [(7.5, 11), (7.6, 10.5), (7.4, 11)], the output should be True.

title: DNA Sequence Analyzer
spec: Write a function `analyze(sequences)` that filters genetic data strings. The standard codon length is three. The minimum required sequence length is twenty one. The maximum allowed gap of continuous dashes is ten. For each sequence in the input list, remove all dash characters to determine the effective length. Reject any sequence whose effective length is not an exact multiple of the standard codon length, or whose effective length is below the minimum length requirement. Additionally, reject any sequence that originally contained a consecutive string of dashes strictly greater than the maximum gap. Return a list of the sequences that pass all checks. For example, given ["ATG-CTA-GGG-TTA-CGC-AAT-TTC", "ATGC", "A" + "-"*12 + "C"], the output should be ["ATG-CTA-GGG-TTA-CGC-AAT-TTC"].

title: Call Center Staffing Predictor
spec: Write a function `staff(volumes)` that estimates hourly manpower needs. The input is a list of expected call counts for consecutive hours. The base required agents is two. The average call duration is three hundred seconds. The maximum agent utilization rate is zero point eight. For each hour, calculate the total expected seconds of work by multiplying the call count by the average duration. Convert this to required hours of work by dividing by thirty six hundred. Divide this by the maximum utilization rate to find the raw agent count. Round this number up to the nearest whole integer and add the base required agents to account for overhead. Return the list of agent counts. For example, given [10, 50, 0], the output should be [4, 8, 2].

title: Wine Fermentation Analyzer
spec: Write a function `ferment(batches)` that calculates alcohol content and viability. The input is a list of tuples containing the starting specific gravity and the ending specific gravity. The target final gravity limit is one point zero. The standard sugar conversion multiplier is one hundred thirty one point twenty five. The minimum acceptable alcohol percentage is ten point zero. The maximum expected alcohol percentage is fifteen point zero. Calculate the alcohol content by subtracting the end gravity from the start gravity, then multiplying by the conversion multiplier. Filter the results: if the end gravity is below the target limit, or the alcohol percentage falls outside the minimum and maximum bounds inclusively, discard the batch. Return a list of the valid alcohol percentages rounded to one decimal place. For example, given [(1.090, 0.995), (1.100, 1.010), (1.050, 1.000)], the output should be [11.8].

title: Satellite Orbit Decay Estimator
spec: Write a function `decay(satellites)` that projects atmospheric drag lifespan. The input is a list of current orbital altitudes in kilometers. The critical safe threshold is two hundred kilometers. The daily base decay rate is fifteen kilometers. The drag coefficient multiplier is one point five. For each satellite, simulate its daily descent. If its altitude is strictly below five hundred kilometers, its daily decay is the base decay rate multiplied by the drag coefficient. Otherwise, its daily decay is just the base decay rate. Count the number of days until the altitude drops strictly below the critical safe threshold. Return a list of integer day counts for each satellite. For example, given [210, 510], the output should be [1, 21].

title: Aquaponics System Balancer
spec: Write a function `balance(tanks)` that evaluates aquatic ecosystem stability. The input is a list of tuples containing tank volume in gallons, fish count, and plant count. The maximum stocking density is zero point five fish per gallon. The base ambient nitrate level is ten parts per million. The nitrate production per fish is five parts per million. The nitrate absorption per plant is three parts per million. The maximum safe nitrate threshold is forty parts per million. For each tank, check if the fish count exceeds the tank volume multiplied by the maximum stocking density. Calculate the final nitrate level by adding the base ambient nitrate to the total fish production, then subtracting the plant absorption. If the stocking density is exceeded, or the final nitrate level is strictly greater than the safe threshold, or the final nitrate drops below zero, the tank is unsafe. Return a list of booleans indicating safety. For example, given [(100, 40, 50), (10, 10, 5)], the output should be [True, False].

title: Coffee Roasting Monitor
spec: Write a function `roast(temperatures)` that classifies bean development based on heat profiles. The input is a list of temperature readings in Fahrenheit taken over a roasting session. The first crack threshold is three hundred eighty five degrees. The second crack threshold is four hundred thirty five degrees. The burn threshold is four hundred fifty degrees. The maximum allowed roast time is twenty readings. If the length of the readings list exceeds the maximum allowed time, or if any temperature meets or exceeds the burn threshold, return the string "ruined". Otherwise, find the maximum temperature reached. If it is below the first crack threshold, return "light". If it is between the first crack and strictly below the second crack threshold, return "medium". If it meets or exceeds the second crack threshold, return "dark". For example, given [300, 350, 390, 410], the output should be "medium".

title: Cryptocurrency transaction fee calculator
spec: Write a transaction fee calculator with the entry function `estimate(transactions)`. A transaction has a size in bytes and a priority level. The logic must use fixed values for the base fee, the cost per byte, the signature overhead size, the maximum allowed block size, and a premium priority multiplier. If a transaction size plus the signature overhead size exceeds the maximum allowed block size, it is rejected. Otherwise, calculate the cost as the base fee plus the total size multiplied by the cost per byte. If the priority is high, multiply the final cost by the premium priority multiplier. For example, given a list of sizes [200, 5000000] and priorities, it should return a list with a calculated fee integer and a rejection message.

title: Laser cutter time estimator
spec: Create an estimation tool for laser cutting jobs using the function `process(jobs)`. A job has a cutting distance and an engraving area. The logic must use fixed rates for the cutting speed, the engraving speed, the startup calibration delay, the cooling phase duration, and the maximum safe continuous operation time. For each job, calculate the active time by dividing the cutting distance by the cutting speed, and the engraving area by the engraving speed. Add the startup calibration delay to find the baseline time. If the active time exceeds the maximum safe continuous operation time, add the cooling phase duration to the total time. For example, given a job with 100 distance and 50 area, it returns a total duration of 45.5 minutes.

title: Geothermal heat pump efficiency
spec: Evaluate the viability of geothermal installations with the function `evaluate(systems)`. A system has a fluid flow rate, a temperature difference, and a loop depth. The logic relies on fixed values for the fluid specific heat capacity, the circulating pump power usage, the baseline efficiency threshold, the maximum drilling depth, and the depth penalty factor. If the loop depth exceeds the maximum drilling depth, mark the system as invalid. Calculate the extracted heat as the flow rate multiplied by the temperature difference and the fluid specific heat capacity. Calculate the pump power as the circulating pump power usage plus the loop depth multiplied by the depth penalty factor. Check if the extracted heat divided by the pump power is greater than the baseline efficiency threshold. For example, given a flow rate of 10 and depth of 200, it returns a boolean indicating efficiency passage.

title: Mountaineering oxygen requirement
spec: Calculate high-altitude oxygen needs using the function `calculate(climbs)`. A climb lists the target altitude, the hours spent at that altitude, and the number of climbers. The logic must use standard values for the sea level oxygen consumption rate, the altitude multiplier factor, the standard cylinder capacity, the critical danger altitude, and the emergency reserve amount. For each climb, if the altitude is below the critical danger altitude, zero oxygen is needed. Otherwise, the consumption rate is the sea level oxygen consumption rate multiplied by the altitude multiplier factor. Total oxygen is the rate times the hours times the climbers, plus the emergency reserve amount. For example, given an altitude of 8000 meters for 10 hours and 2 climbers, it returns the number of standard cylinders required as 5.

title: Water purification system monitor
spec: Monitor drinking water filtration using the function `analyze(readings)`. A reading has a particle count, a chlorine level, a flow rate, and a gallons used counter. The logic checks against fixed standards for the maximum allowable particle count, the minimum required chlorine level, the backwash trigger volume, the minimum acceptable flow rate, and the total filter lifespan. If the particle count exceeds the maximum allowable particle count or the chlorine level is below the minimum required chlorine level, the water is flagged as unsafe. If the flow rate drops below the minimum acceptable flow rate, add the backwash trigger volume to the required maintenance tasks. If the gallons used counter exceeds the total filter lifespan, flag for immediate replacement. For example, given a reading of 500 particles and low flow, it returns a list of maintenance alerts.

title: Hovercraft skirt pressure monitor
spec: Regulate lifting fans on a hovercraft with the function `regulate(readings)`. A reading includes the current lift fan speed, the internal skirt pressure, and the terrain roughness score. The system uses fixed parameters for the optimal cushion pressure, the maximum leakage rate, the obstacle clearance pressure, the emergency blower speed, and the pressure loss threshold. Calculate the pressure deficit compared to the optimal cushion pressure. If the deficit indicates a loss greater than the maximum leakage rate, calculate a recommended increase in fan speed. If the terrain roughness score is high, verify the pressure exceeds the obstacle clearance pressure. If pressure falls below the pressure loss threshold, trigger the emergency blower speed. For example, given a pressure of 12 and rough terrain, it returns the adjusted fan speed of 3500.

title: Glassblowing furnace scheduler
spec: Schedule artisan glass processing times using the function `schedule(pieces)`. A piece specifies its mass in kilograms and complexity level. The scheduling depends on fixed parameters for the silica melting temperature, the working shaping temperature, the annealing cooling rate, the ambient studio temperature, and the base heating duration. The time to melt is the base heating duration multiplied by the mass. The shaping time adds a drop period calculated as the silica melting temperature minus the working shaping temperature, divided by a constant factor. The annealing time is the working shaping temperature minus the ambient studio temperature, divided by the annealing cooling rate. For example, given a 5 kilogram piece, it returns a total scheduled processing time of 14.2 hours.

title: Sailboat regatta handicap
spec: Calculate adjusted race scores for sailboats using the function `handicap(boats)`. A boat provides its length, sail area, and displacement weight. The handicap calculation uses fixed values for the baseline standard length, the sail area performance factor, the heavy displacement penalty, the maximum allowed wind speed, and the overall rating multiplier. Calculate a raw score by taking the length minus the baseline standard length, adding the sail area multiplied by the sail area performance factor, and subtracting the displacement weight multiplied by the heavy displacement penalty. Multiply this raw score by the overall rating multiplier. If a global race wind reading exceeds the maximum allowed wind speed, all handicaps are voided. For example, given lengths of 30 and 40 feet, it returns handicap ratings of 1.15 and 1.02.

title: Maple syrup boiling process
spec: Predict the time and temperature for sap reduction using the function `boil(batches)`. A batch contains the starting volume of sap and its initial sugar percentage. The logic requires standard constants for the target finished syrup density, the boiling point elevation per sugar degree, the water evaporation rate per hour, the filtering temperature threshold, and the minimum sap sugar threshold. If the initial sugar percentage is below the minimum sap sugar threshold, discard the batch. Calculate the required water to remove by comparing the initial sugar percentage to the target finished syrup density. The time required is the water to remove divided by the water evaporation rate per hour. Verify the final boiling temperature exceeds the filtering temperature threshold. For example, given 100 gallons of sap at 2 percent sugar, it returns a boil time of 8.5 hours.

title: Cheese aging cave climate control
spec: Manage subterranean aging environments using the function `ventilate(caves)`. Each cave reports its current humidity, ammonia parts per million, and temperature. The climate system relies on fixed limits for the optimal target humidity, the maximum safe ammonia level, the upper temperature bound, the lower temperature bound, and the standard fan runtime. If the humidity falls below the optimal target humidity, output an instruction to activate the misting system. If the ammonia exceeds the maximum safe ammonia level, output an instruction to activate the exhaust for the standard fan runtime. If the temperature goes above the upper temperature bound or below the lower temperature bound, output climate heating or cooling commands. For example, given high ammonia and low temperature, it returns a list containing exhaust and heater activation commands.

title: Perfume blending ratio
spec: Formulate exact liquid volumes for fragrance production using the function `blend(formulas)`. A formula gives the desired total volume and a fragrance concentration category. The blending logic applies fixed ratios for the top note percentage, the heart note percentage, the base note percentage, the alcohol dilution factor for standard concentration, and the resting maceration days. Calculate the pure fragrance oil volume by multiplying the total volume by the alcohol dilution factor for standard concentration. Subdivide the oil volume using the top note percentage, the heart note percentage, and the base note percentage. The formula output should list these liquid volumes and append the resting maceration days. For example, given a target volume of 100 milliliters, it returns the three note volumes as 15, 20, and 5, alongside 30 days of resting.

title: Pottery kiln firing schedule
spec: Determine the heating curve for ceramics using the function `fire(programs)`. A program specifies the clay type and the thickness of the piece. The firing schedule relies on standard settings for the bisque peak temperature, the glaze peak temperature, the gradual ramp up rate, the peak holding time, and the safety shutoff temperature. If the clay is marked as raw, target the bisque peak temperature; otherwise target the glaze peak temperature. Calculate the hours to reach the target using the gradual ramp up rate multiplied by a thickness factor. Add the peak holding time. If the target exceeds the safety shutoff temperature, cap the target at the safety maximum. title: Hot air balloon lift capacity
spec: Evaluate safe flight parameters for ballooning with the function `capacity(flights)`. A flight has an envelope volume, an outside air temperature, and a passenger count. The lift model uses fixed parameters for the sea level air density, the burner maximum heat output, the standard passenger weight, the fabric safe temperature limit, and the required safety lift margin. Calculate the total passenger weight using the standard passenger weight. Determine the internal temperature needed to generate lift based on the sea level air density and the envelope volume. If the required temperature exceeds the fabric safe temperature limit or requires more heat than the burner maximum heat output, mark the flight as canceled. For example, given 4 passengers and a small volume, it returns a cancellation warning due to heat limits.

title: Hydroponic nutrient doser
spec: Automate fertilizer delivery in a greenhouse using the function `dose(readings)`. A reading gives the current acidity level, the electrical conductivity, and the water reservoir volume. The dosing logic uses fixed targets for the ideal acidity level, the acidity tolerance band, the nutrient concentration factor, the pump dispensing rate, and the full system flush volume. If the acidity is outside the ideal acidity level plus or minus the acidity tolerance band, calculate the ph adjuster amount and divide by the pump dispensing rate for the run time. Use the electrical conductivity and the nutrient concentration factor to find the nutrient dose volume. title: Commercial laundry wash cycles
spec: Program industrial washing machines with the function `wash(loads)`. A load specifies its weight in kilograms, soil level, and fabric type. The machine operation depends on fixed parameters for the hot water temperature, the detergent dose per kilogram, the maximum extraction gravity force, the delicate spin speed limit, and the baseline standard cycle duration. If the soil level is heavy, use the hot water temperature; otherwise use cold. The soap amount is the weight multiplied by the detergent dose per kilogram. For delicate fabrics, cap the spin at the delicate spin speed limit; otherwise use the maximum extraction gravity force. Add processing time to the baseline standard cycle duration based on the weight. For example, given a 10 kilogram heavy load, it returns a 60 minute duration with 50 grams of detergent.

title: Soap making saponification
spec: Calculate chemical reactant values for cold process soap using the function `saponify(recipes)`. A recipe details the grams of olive oil, coconut oil, and palm oil. The chemical calculation requires fixed constants for the olive oil lye multiplier, the coconut oil lye multiplier, the standard water ratio, the superfat discount percentage, and the minimum curing weeks. Calculate the water needed by multiplying the total oil weight by the standard water ratio. title: Dry cleaning solvent recycling
spec: Manage fluid distillation in dry cleaning equipment with the function `distill(cycles)`. A cycle records the used solvent volume, the sludge concentration, and the operating vacuum level. Apply the recovery efficiency rate to the solvent volume to find the purified yield. If the sludge concentration exceeds the sludge warning threshold, flag for immediate maintenance. title: Wind tunnel aerodynamics tester
spec: Process force readings from aerodynamic scale models using the function `test(models)`. A model specifies its frontal area, measured drag force, and measured lift force. If any force fluctuates by more than the sensor calibration variance threshold during the test window, mark the results as unreliable. title: Bronze casting foundry
spec: Coordinate molten metal pours with the function `cast(molds)`. A mold specifies its internal volume and the ambient temperature. The pouring process depends on fixed constants for the bronze melting point, the crucible preheat temperature, the maximum pouring duration, the thermal shrinkage rate, and the mold cooling time. Calculate the required molten metal volume by adding the thermal shrinkage rate to the initial mold volume. Ensure the furnace is instructed to heat to the bronze melting point while maintaining the crucible preheat temperature. The pour must be completed within the maximum pouring duration to avoid cold shuts. For example, given a volume of 10 liters, it returns a required metal volume of 10.5 liters and a mandated rest period matching the mold cooling time.

title: Cable car wire tension
spec: Monitor the structural limits of an aerial tramway using the function `inspect(spans)`. Each span reports its current passenger count, wind speed, and span distance. The monitoring system evaluates safety against fixed constants for the maximum passenger load limit, the cable stretch tolerance limit, the wind warning threshold, the emergency braking force, and the baseline empty tension. Calculate total tension by adding the baseline empty tension to the passenger count multiplied by standard weight. If the distance implies a stretch beyond the cable stretch tolerance limit, or the passenger count exceeds the maximum passenger load limit, trigger a critical alert. If wind speed exceeds the wind warning threshold, recommend applying the emergency braking force. For example, given 50 passengers and high wind, it returns an alert and braking command.

title: Fireworks display timing
spec: Generate ignition schedules for pyrotechnics using the function `sequence(shells)`. A shell has a diameter size, a launch angle, and a visual effect type. The launch computer uses standard physical constants for the fuse burn speed, the mortar lift velocity, the average burst altitude per inch, the spectator safety radius, and the standard delay buffer. Calculate the ignition lead time by dividing the fuse length by the fuse burn speed. Calculate the time in air using the mortar lift velocity and the average burst altitude per inch. Ensure the calculated fallout zone does not overlap with the spectator safety radius. For example, given a 6 inch shell and a 4 inch shell, it returns a list of precise ignition timestamps separated by the standard delay buffer.

title: Meat smoking temperature and time
spec: Estimate barbecue cooking durations with the function `smoke(cuts)`. A cut of meat specifies its weight in pounds, its type, and its current internal temperature. The pitmaster algorithm relies on fixed targets for the ideal smoker ambient temperature, the target done temperature, the moisture stall start temperature, the typical stall duration, and the foil wrap threshold. Calculate base cooking time from the weight. If the internal temperature hits the moisture stall start temperature, add the typical stall duration to the estimate. If the temperature exceeds the foil wrap threshold, output an instruction to wrap the meat. For example, given a 10 pound brisket at 165 degrees, it returns an instruction to wrap and maintain the pit at the ideal smoker ambient temperature.

title: Bungee jumping physics
spec: Verify elastic line parameters for extreme sports using the function `jump(clients)`. A client provides their weight and the desired platform height. The jump calculation uses fixed parameters for the cord elasticity coefficient, the maximum safe stretch length, the freefall gravity acceleration, the harness breaking load limit, and the ground safety clearance. Calculate the freefall kinetic energy using the weight, the platform height, and the freefall gravity acceleration. Determine the stretch distance using the cord elasticity coefficient. Check that the peak force does not exceed the harness breaking load limit. Ensure the platform height minus the stretch leaves at least the ground safety clearance. For example, given a client of 80 kilograms, it returns the maximum stretch distance and a safety clearance boolean.

title: Pickle brining process
spec: Determine acid and salt concentrations for food preservation using the function `brine(cucumbers)`. A batch specifies the cucumber weight and the desired sourness level. The recipe relies on standard values for the base salt percentage, the vinegar dilution ratio, the minimum fermentation days, the spoilage temperature threshold, and the calcium chloride crispness additive. Calculate the salt weight using the base salt percentage against the cucumber weight. Determine the vinegar and water volumes using the vinegar dilution ratio based on the desired sourness. Add a fixed amount of the calcium chloride crispness additive to maintain texture. For example, given 5 kilograms of cucumbers, it returns the required salt and vinegar amounts, and ensures the batch is held for the minimum fermentation days.

title: Textile dyeing process
spec: Calculate chemical loads for fabric coloring with the function `dye(fabrics)`. A fabric run specifies its dry weight, material type, and desired shade depth. The dye house automation uses fixed amounts for the base dye per kilogram, the required water per kilogram, the standard boiling time, the chemical fixative ratio, and the minimum rinse cycles. Calculate the total dye needed by multiplying the weight by the base dye per kilogram and scaling by the shade depth. Calculate the water needed using the required water per kilogram. Determine the fixative amount using the chemical fixative ratio applied to the total dye. For example, given 100 kilograms of cotton, it returns the total dye, water volume, and verifies the process ends with the minimum rinse cycles.

Example input: [(20, 1, False)]. Output: [12.19].

The subtotal must meet a minimum service call charge of 100 dollars before adding a travel fee of 1.50 dollars per mile. Return a list of total costs. Example input: [(2, False, False, 10)]. Output: [115.0].

spec: Implement a function `shampoo(jobs)` to price carpet cleaning jobs given as tuples of square meters, number of stairs, and number of stubborn stains. title: Plumber Invoice

title: Hair Salon Booking
spec: Create a function `salon(appointments)` to calculate hair service charges from tuples of service duration in minutes, a boolean for premium stylist, and a boolean for coloring.
