title: Ski Equipment Rental
spec: Implement a function `ski(rentals)` to price winter sports gear from tuples of days rented, a boolean for premium skis, and a boolean for helmet rental. The daily ski rate is 30 dollars for base skis or 50 dollars for premium skis, capped at a maximum rental duration of 14 days. Helmet rentals cost 10 dollars per day, a mandatory insurance waiver of 5 dollars per day applies, and rentals exceeding 4 days receive a 15 percent long term discount. Return a list of totals. Example input: [(3, False, True)]. Output: [135.0].

title: Dumpster Rental
spec: Create a function `dumpster(rentals)` to calculate waste container costs from tuples of container size in yards, days rented, and tons of waste disposed. The daily rental fee is 15 dollars capped at 30 days, the base delivery fee is 100 dollars, and waste disposal costs 60 dollars per ton. The maximum weight allowance is 4 tons, with any excess weight incurring a severe penalty of 90 dollars per ton. Return a list of total invoices. Example input: [(10, 5, 2)]. Output: [295.0].

title: Paper Mill Production
spec: A paper mill roll has length, speed, moisture, width, and defects. Normal paper width is four hundred. Ideal moisture is five. Base machine speed limit is one thousand. Absolute maximum speed is twelve hundred. Each defect reduces the grade by five points from a perfect starting score of one hundred. Rolls exceeding the base speed limit incur a double defect penalty of ten points per defect, and exceeding the absolute maximum immediately returns a score of zero. Write the function `evaluate(rolls)` to process a list of rolls. Return a list of tuples containing the final score and a boolean indicating if it passed by having a score strictly greater than seventy. Example input: `[(2000, 1100, 5, 400, 2)]`. Output: `[(80, True)]`.

title: Air Traffic Separation
spec: Air traffic control tracks aircraft pairs with their altitude difference, lateral distance, and heavy wake flag. Minimum vertical separation is one thousand. Minimum lateral separation is five. A heavy aircraft wake penalty increases required lateral separation by two. The speed warning difference is fifty. The base safety score is ten. Deduct one from the base safety score for every whole unit of lateral distance under the requirement. If vertical separation is under the minimum, the score becomes zero. Write the function `monitor(aircraft)` to evaluate a list of aircraft pairs. Return a list of safety scores and a boolean warning flag which is True if the score is under five. Example input: `[(800, 4, True)]`. Output: `[(0, True)]`.

title: Tea Oxidation Process
spec: Tea fermentation monitoring uses temperature, humidity, and time. Green tea maximum temperature is eighty. Oolong optimal humidity is sixty. Black tea minimum time is one hundred twenty. The temperature penalty is ten points for being over the maximum. The humidity penalty is five points for being under optimal. The perfect base score is one hundred. Write the function `grade(batches)` to process a list of batches given as type, temperature, humidity, and time. Start at the perfect base score, apply the temperature penalty if it is green tea over the maximum, apply the humidity penalty if oolong is under optimal, and fail it with a score of zero if black tea is under the minimum time. Return a list of final scores and a pass boolean if the score is above seventy. Example input: `[('green', 82, 50, 100)]`. Output: `[(90, True)]`.

title: Helicopter Logging Payload
spec: Helicopter logging payload calculations use wood types and volumes. Maximum sling capacity is four thousand. Pine density is forty. Oak density is fifty. Fuel reserve weight is five hundred. The safety margin is ten percent of the total calculated wood weight. Write the function `plan(trees)` to process a list of trees containing type and volume. Calculate wood weight as volume times the specific density. Add the fuel reserve and the safety margin to get the total load. Return a list of total loads and a boolean indicating if it is under or equal to the maximum sling capacity. Example input: `[('pine', 50)]`. Output: `[(2700.0, True)]`.

title: Truffle Hunting Yield
spec: Truffle hunting yields depend on soil acidity and dog stamina. White truffle value is two hundred. Black truffle value is eighty. Maximum dog fatigue limit is four. Ideal soil acidity is seven. Acidity penalty is zero point five. The base hourly find rate is ten. Write the function `estimate(zones)` to process a list containing type, acidity, and hours. Calculate hours used as the minimum of planned hours and the fatigue limit. Calculate find rate as the base rate minus the absolute difference between acidity and ideal, multiplied by the penalty. Total value is hours used times find rate times the truffle value. Return a list of total values and a boolean if the fatigue limit was reached. Example input: `[('white', 8, 5)]`. Output: `[(7600.0, True)]`.

title: Subway Ventilation
spec: Subway ventilation adjusts to passenger levels. Carbon dioxide threshold is eight hundred. Emergency purge level is twelve hundred. Normal fan speed is thirty. High fan speed is eighty. Base air exchange rate is five. Maximum passenger limit is five hundred. Write the function `regulate(stations)` to process a list of passenger counts and carbon dioxide levels. If passengers exceed the limit, add two hundred to the carbon dioxide reading. If the adjusted carbon dioxide exceeds the purge level, the speed is high fan speed plus twenty. If it exceeds the threshold, speed is high fan speed. Otherwise, speed is normal fan speed. Return a list of fan speeds and a boolean if the emergency purge was triggered. Example input: `[(600, 1100)]`. Output: `[(100, True)]`.

title: Bowling Lane Oil
spec: Bowling lane oil patterns break down with play. Heavy oil starting volume is twenty five. Light oil starting volume is ten. Buff area length is forty. Breakdown rate per game is zero point two. Minimum acceptable volume is five. Write the function `analyze(lanes)` to process a list of pattern strings and games played. Start with the starting volume for that pattern. Subtract the breakdown rate times games played. If games played exceed the buff length, subtract an additional two units. Return a list of remaining volumes and a boolean if the volume is strictly below the minimum acceptable volume. Example input: `[('heavy', 10)]`. Output: `[(23.0, False)]`.

title: Telescope Mirror Polishing
spec: Telescope mirror polishing schedules use initial grit and pressure. Coarse grit size is eighty. Fine grit size is four hundred. Maximum safe pressure is fifteen. Optimal stroke speed is thirty. Base polishing time is sixty. Edge defect penalty is twenty. Write the function `schedule(mirrors)` to process a list of grit, pressure, and defect counts. Start with the base time. If grit is coarse, add forty to time. If pressure exceeds the safe maximum, halve the total time but flag a warning. Add the edge defect penalty multiplied by the number of defects. Return a list of total times and the warning boolean. Example input: `[(80, 10, 2)]`. Output: `[(140.0, False)]`.

title: Pearl Farming Yield
spec: Pearl farming uses water temperature and time to estimate nacre growth. Ideal water temperature is twenty four. Bead rejection rate is fifteen. Standard maturation time is twenty four. Base nacre thickness is two. Cold water penalty is zero point five. Premium size threshold is three. Write the function `forecast(oysters)` to process a list of temperatures and months submerged. If months are less than half the standard time, thickness is zero. Otherwise, start with base nacre thickness, add zero point one for every month over the standard time, and subtract the cold water penalty if temperature is strictly below ideal. Return a list of final thicknesses and a boolean if it meets or exceeds the premium threshold. Example input: `[(22, 26)]`. Output: `[(1.7, False)]`.

title: Snowboard Halfpipe Shaping
spec: Snowboard halfpipe safety evaluates dimensions and snow density. Standard wall height is twenty two. Minimum flat width is fifteen. Optimal transition radius is sixteen. Snow density target is five hundred. Soft snow penalty is ten. Perfect safety score is one hundred. Write the function `validate(pipes)` to process a list of heights, widths, and densities. Start at perfect safety score. Deduct five for every unit the height is below standard. Deduct five for every unit the width is below minimum. If density is below target, deduct the soft snow penalty. Return a list of safety scores and a boolean if the score is above eighty. Example input: `[(20, 15, 450)]`. Output: `[(80, False)]`.

title: Racecar Pit Stop
spec: Racecar pit stop efficiency evaluates crew speed and penalties. Base tire change time is two. Fuel flow rate is twelve. Pit lane speed limit is eighty. Speeding penalty is five. Jack drop time is zero point five. Maximum crew size is twenty. Write the function `evaluate(stops)` to process a list of incoming speeds, fuel needed, and crew sizes. Calculate fuel time as fuel needed divided by fuel flow rate. Stationary time is the maximum of fuel time and base tire change time, plus jack drop time. Add one second if crew size is under maximum. Add the speeding penalty if incoming speed exceeds the limit. Return a list of total times and a boolean if a penalty was applied. Example input: `[(85, 24, 20)]`. Output: `[(7.5, True)]`.

title: Lighthouse Optics
spec: Lighthouse optics adjust based on visibility and battery level. Warning flash interval is ten. Emergency flash interval is three. Base candela is one million. Fog multiplier is two. Maximum rotation speed is six. Minimum battery reserve is twenty. Write the function `configure(lights)` to process a list of visibility distances and battery levels. If battery is below the reserve, candela is halved and interval is the warning flash interval regardless of visibility. Otherwise, if visibility is under two, candela is base candela multiplied by the fog multiplier and interval is the emergency flash interval. Default is base candela and warning flash interval. Return a list of candela and interval pairs. Example input: `[(1, 25)]`. Output: `[(2000000, 3)]`.

title: Falconry Training
spec: Falconry training progress is evaluated by weight and flight. Target hunting weight is eight hundred. Minimum flight distance is fifty. Optimal lure speed is thirty. Weight variance penalty is five. Perfect readiness score is one hundred. Minimum pass score is eighty. Write the function `assess(birds)` to process a list of weights and distances. Start with perfect readiness score. Deduct the variance penalty for every ten units of absolute difference between weight and target hunting weight. Deduct ten if distance is below minimum flight distance. Return a list of scores and a boolean if the score is at least the minimum pass score. Example input: `[(820, 60)]`. Output: `[(90, True)]`.

title: Ice Sculpting
spec: Ice sculpting calculates time and risks based on conditions. Standard block height is forty. Chainsaw cut rate is five. Chisel detail limit is two. Melting temperature threshold is thirty two. Ambient penalty multiplier is one point one. Base setup time is fifteen. Write the function `carve(blocks)` to process a list containing feet to cut, detail hours, and temperatures. Base time is setup time plus feet times chainsaw cut rate, plus detail hours times sixty. If temperature exceeds the threshold, multiply total time by the ambient penalty multiplier. Return a list of total times and a boolean if detail hours exceed the limit. Example input: `[(10, 1, 35)]`. Output: `[(137.5, False)]`.

title: Snooker Break Building
spec: Snooker break scoring depends on ball values and fouls. Red ball value is one. Black ball value is seven. Standard table length is twelve. Maximum cue power is ten. Foul penalty is four. Write the function `score(shots)` to process a list of turns, where each turn is a list of tuples containing ball color strings and foul booleans. Sum the values of red or black balls in the turn. If a foul occurred on any shot in the turn, subtract the foul penalty from the turn's total score. Ignore other ball colors. Return a list of total turn scores and a boolean if the score is negative. Example input: `[[('red', False), ('black', False), ('red', True)]]`. Output: `[(5, False)]`.

title: Sushi Rice Preparation
spec: Sushi rice preparation requires exact ingredient ratios. Optimal vinegar ratio is zero point one. Optimal sugar ratio is zero point zero five. Target cooling temperature is thirty five. Standard hydration time is thirty. Temperature variance penalty is two. Starting quality score is fifty. Write the function `prepare(batches)` to process rice weight, vinegar weight, sugar weight, and temperature. Deduct the absolute difference between vinegar weight and rice weight times optimal vinegar ratio. Deduct the absolute difference between sugar weight and rice weight times optimal sugar ratio. Deduct the temperature variance penalty for every degree off the target temperature. Return a list of quality scores and a boolean if the score is strictly above zero. Example input: `[(1000, 100, 50, 37)]`. Output: `[(46.0, True)]`.

title: Typewriter Mechanics
spec: Typewriter mechanical repair scores evaluate part tolerances. Ideal platen hardness is ninety. Optimal key travel distance is fifteen. Minimum ribbon tension is five. Margin bell warning threshold is ten. Hardness variance deduction is zero point five. Maximum service score is one hundred. Write the function `repair(machines)` to process hardness, travel, and tension values. Start at maximum service score. Deduct the absolute difference between hardness and ideal platen hardness multiplied by the deduction. Deduct five if travel is not optimal. Return a list of service scores and a replacement boolean which is True if tension is strictly below minimum ribbon tension. Example input: `[(80, 15, 4)]`. Output: `[(95.0, True)]`.

title: Hot Dog Contest
spec: Hot dog eating contests score competitors on intake minus penalties. Regulation time limit is ten. Standard hot dog weight is one hundred. Bun weight is thirty. Reversal penalty is twenty. Minimum consumption for rank is five. Base score multiplier is ten. Write the function `judge(eaters)` to process a list of dogs eaten and reversal counts. Total score is dogs eaten times base score multiplier, minus reversals times reversal penalty. Return a list of total scores and a boolean if dogs eaten meets the minimum consumption. Example input: `[(8, 1)]`. Output: `[(60, True)]`.

title: Glider Winch Launching
spec: Glider winch launching requires tension and speed control. Maximum cable tension is ten. Optimal pull speed is fifty. Standard release altitude is one thousand. Weak link break strain is twelve. Headwind bonus altitude is twenty. Base launch time is forty. Write the function `launch(gliders)` to process a list of wind speed, mass, and target altitude. Calculate tension as mass divided by one hundred. If tension exceeds maximum cable tension, cap it at maximum. Calculate estimated launch time as base launch time plus the target altitude minus the wind speed times headwind bonus, all divided by ten. Return a list of tension and time pairs. Example input: `[(10, 500, 1200)]`. Output: `[(5.0, 140.0)]`.

title: Bonsai Tree Wiring
spec: Bonsai tree wiring recommends wire gauge and recovery time. Heavy wire gauge is four. Light wire gauge is one. Maximum branch bend angle is forty five. Standard recovery weeks is twelve. Overbend penalty weeks is four. Target aesthetics score is ten. Write the function `shape(trees)` to process a list of thickness and bend angles. If thickness is over five, use the heavy wire gauge, otherwise light wire gauge. If bend angle exceeds maximum, add overbend penalty weeks to standard recovery, and reduce target aesthetics score by two. Return a list of tuples containing recommended gauge, recovery weeks, and aesthetics score. Example input: `[(6, 50)]`. Output: `[(4, 16, 8)]`.

title: Harp Tuning Strings
spec: Harp string tuning evaluates pitch and tension. Base concert pitch is four hundred forty. Maximum string tension is forty. Minimum gut thickness is zero point five. Nylon stretch factor is zero point zero two. Pitch variance warning is five. Write the function `tune(strings)` to process a list of material string, pitch, and tension. If material is nylon, allowed variance is pitch variance warning plus ten; otherwise it is just pitch variance warning. If the absolute difference between pitch and base concert pitch exceeds allowed variance, or if tension exceeds maximum string tension, flag a warning. Return a list of pitch differences and the warning boolean. Example input: `[('gut', 430, 35)]`. Output: `[(10, True)]`.

title: Neon Sign Bending
spec: Neon sign bending calculates fill pressure and voltage. Argon fill pressure is twelve. Neon fill pressure is fifteen. Glass melting point is eight hundred. Base electrode voltage is three thousand. Color penalty multiplier is zero point nine. Standard tube length is ten. Write the function `fabricate(tubes)` to process gas types and lengths. Pressure is the argon or neon pressure based on gas type. Voltage is base electrode voltage plus length times one hundred. If length exceeds standard tube length, multiply the final brightness score of one hundred by the color penalty multiplier. Return a list of pressure, voltage, and brightness tuples. Example input: `[('neon', 12)]`. Output: `[(15, 4200, 90.0)]`.

title: Jousting Tournament
spec: Jousting tournaments score passes based on strikes and horsemanship. Lance break points are three. Shield strike points are one. Unhorse points are ten. Minimum horse speed is fifteen. Slow penalty is two. Perfect pass score is zero. Write the function `score(passes)` to process a list of strike types and speeds. Add points based on the strike type string being break, shield, or unhorse. If speed is strictly below the minimum horse speed, subtract the slow penalty. Return a list of total pass scores and a boolean indicating if the pass was a valid unhorse, meaning it was an unhorse with no slow penalty. Example input: `[('unhorse', 14)]`. Output: `[(8, False)]`.

title: Llama Packing Trek
spec: Llama packing treks evaluate daily limits and load. Maximum saddlebag weight is twenty five. Daily distance limit is fifteen. Base hydration requirement is five. Altitude multiplier is one point five. Overweight penalty distance is two. Starting health score is one hundred. Write the function `pack(llamas)` to process a list of weights and altitudes. If weight exceeds maximum, reduce daily distance limit by the penalty and deduct ten from health score. Hydration is base requirement; multiply it by the altitude multiplier if altitude exceeds ten thousand. Return a list of allowed distance, hydration, and health score. Example input: `[(26, 12000)]`. Output: `[(13, 7.5, 90)]`.

title: Paragliding Thermalling
spec: Paragliding thermalling safety uses climb rates and limits. Minimum climb rate is two. Dangerous sink rate is negative five. Maximum bank angle is forty. Stall speed warning is twenty. Cloud base limit is five thousand. Perfect safety score is one hundred. Write the function `soar(flights)` to process altitudes, climbs, banks, and speeds. Deduct ten from the safety score if climb is below dangerous sink rate. Deduct twenty if bank angle exceeds maximum. If altitude exceeds cloud base limit or speed is below stall speed warning, set score to zero. Return a list of safety scores and a boolean if the score is perfect. Example input: `[(4000, -6, 45, 25)]`. Output: `[(70, False)]`.

title: Watch Repair Estimation
spec: Write a program with the main entry point `estimate(repairs)`. The input is a list of tuples containing the repair type as a string and the watch brand tier as an integer from one to three. Base labor cost is fifty. A cleaning is twenty five. A spring replacement is forty. A glass replacement is sixty. A tier two brand adds a thirty percent multiplier to the total. A tier three luxury brand adds an eighty percent multiplier. The minimum total charge is always one hundred. Handle cleaning, spring, and glass repairs. Return a list of final costs. Example input: [('spring', 2)], output: [117.0].

title: Candle Making Wax Calculator
spec: Implement a script with the function `formulate(candles)`. The input is a list of tuples providing candle volume in milliliters and scent strength as a string which can be light, medium, or strong. The base wax density is zero point nine grams per milliliter. A light scent requires three percent of the volume in fragrance oil. A medium scent requires six percent. A strong scent needs ten percent. A melting loss factor of five percent is added to the required wax weight. A glass jar safety margin of ten milliliters is subtracted from the usable volume. Return a list of tuples with total wax weight and total fragrance oil volume needed for each. Example input: [(110, 'medium')], output: [(94.5, 6.0)].

title: Conveyor Belt Power Consumption
spec: Create a module with the function `calculate(traffic)`. The input is a list of integers representing the number of items per minute on a conveyor belt. The base empty motor power is five thousand watts. Each item adds one hundred and fifty watts of load. A standby mode activates if the belt is empty, dropping the power to one thousand watts. The maximum motor capacity is fifteen thousand watts. A maintenance warning threshold is triggered if power exceeds twelve thousand watts. Return a list of tuples containing the power used and a boolean indicating if the maintenance threshold or capacity was exceeded. Example input: [0, 10, 100], output: [(1000, False), (6500, False), (15000, True)].

title: Fountain Pen Ink Capacity
spec: Develop a tool with the entry function `evaluate(pens)`. The input is a list of tuples containing pen model string, reservoir length in millimeters, and reservoir diameter in millimeters. The total volume is calculated using pi times the radius squared times the length. Assume pi is exactly three point one four. The usable volume is eighty five percent of the total volume. A standard nib consumes zero point zero two cubic millimeters per page. A broad nib consumes zero point zero four. An evaporation loss of five percent is deducted from the usable volume. Compute the number of pages each pen can write assuming a standard nib, capped at a maximum page limit of five hundred. Return a list of integers representing the pages. Example input: [('Alpha', 50, 5)], output: [500].

title: Vinyl Record Pressing Cycle
spec: Write a scheduler starting with `schedule(orders)`. The input is a list of integer quantities for different album runs. The machine warmup phase takes thirty minutes. Each individual record takes forty five seconds to press. A cooling phase is required per batch of five hundred records, taking twenty minutes. The defect rate assumption is three percent, so the target press quantity must increase by this margin. The maximum continuous run time is four hundred and eighty minutes before a mandatory sixty minute maintenance period is triggered. Calculate the total minutes needed for each order independently and return them in a list. Example input: [100], output: [107.25].

title: Rainwater Harvesting Tank
spec: Build a simulator with the function `forecast(rainfall)`. The input is a list of daily rainfall amounts in millimeters. The roof area is one hundred and twenty square meters. The collection efficiency is eighty percent. A first flush system diverts the first ten liters of rain per day. The storage tank capacity is five thousand liters. The daily household usage is one hundred and fifty liters. For each day, add the collected water to the tank, subtract usage, and cap at the maximum capacity. Initially the tank has five hundred liters. Return a tuple containing the number of days the tank overflows and the final volume at the end of the period. Example input: [10, 0, 5], output: (0, 1300.0).

title: Septic Tank Pumping Schedule
spec: Design an analyzer with the function `analyze(households)`. The input is a list of tuples containing tank volume in gallons and the number of occupants. The base accumulation rate is sixty gallons per person per year. A volume safety threshold dictates that the tank must be pumped when the sludge reaches thirty five percent of the total capacity. A garbage disposal adds twenty percent to the accumulation rate. The minimum pumping interval is one year, and the maximum allowed interval by code is ten years. Assume all households use a disposal. A base inspection fee of fifty is charged per year. Return a list of tuples with the recommended pumping intervals in years, truncated to the nearest integer, and the lifetime inspection fee up to that interval. Example input: [(1000, 4)], output: [(1, 50)].

title: Kitesurfing Wind Tolerance
spec: Implement an assessor using the entry `assess(conditions)`. The input is a list of tuples containing wind speed in knots and rider weight in kilograms. The minimum wind required is twelve knots and the maximum safe wind is thirty knots. The base kite size for a seventy five kilogram rider at twenty knots is ten square meters. For every five kilograms over the base weight, add zero point five square meters. For every two knots under the base wind speed, add one square meter. If the wind is outside the safe limits, return the string unsafe instead of a number. Return a list of results. Example input: [(18, 80), (10, 75)], output: [11.5, 'unsafe'].

title: Pothole Repair Asphalt Calculator
spec: Write a script with the function `measure(potholes)`. The input is a list of tuples providing the diameter in centimeters and depth in centimeters of various potholes. The asphalt density is two point three grams per cubic centimeter. Assume a cylindrical volume and that pi is three point one four. A compaction factor requires fifteen percent extra volume. The minimum patch weight is five kilograms. The maximum single truck payload is two thousand kilograms. A transport loss of two kilograms per truck is subtracted from the payload capacity. Compute the total weight in kilograms required for all potholes. Return a tuple of the number of trucks needed and the total weight of asphalt required. Example input: [(50, 10)], output: (1, 51.9).

title: Skateboard Ramp Geometry
spec: Create a geometric calculator starting with `design(ramps)`. The input is a list of ramp heights in meters. The transition arc length is estimated as the height multiplied by one point five seven. The flat bottom minimum length is three meters. The top deck length is one point two meters. The standard width of the ramp is two point four meters. The total surface area is the width multiplied by the sum of the arc length, flat bottom, and deck. The base wood thickness required is eighteen millimeters. Compute the total wood volume in cubic meters for each ramp by multiplying the area by the thickness. Return a list of volumes. Example input: [2.0], output: [0.317].

title: Chimney Sweeping Soot Volume
spec: Develop a tool with the function `estimate(chimneys)`. The input is a list of tuples containing flue length in meters, years since the last clean, and wood type as a string which is either hardwood or softwood. Hardwood produces zero point five liters of soot per meter per year. Softwood produces one point two liters. The baseline blockage risk threshold is ten liters. The base cleaning fee is eighty. Add fifteen for every liter above the baseline risk threshold. A safety inspection fee of twenty is always added. Return a list of total fees for each chimney. Example input: [(5, 2, 'hardwood')], output: [100.0].

title: Fencing Match Scoring
spec: Implement a scoring module with the entry `score(bouts)`. The input is a list of tuples containing the fencer touches, opponent touches, and penalty cards received. The target score to win a bout is fifteen touches. Each penalty card deducts one touch from the fencer score. A dominant win occurs when winning by five or more touches and earns three ranking points. A standard win earns two points. A loss earns zero points. A draw earns one point. The adjusted score cannot drop below zero. Return a list of ranking points earned by the fencer for each bout. Example input: [(15, 8, 1), (12, 15, 0)], output: [3, 0].

title: Rugby Scrum Push Force
spec: Write a physics model with the function `simulate(scrums)`. The input is a list of tuples providing total pack weight in kilograms and average boot stud length in millimeters. The base push force is the pack weight multiplied by one point five newtons per kilogram. The optimal stud length is eighteen millimeters. For every millimeter under the optimal length, deduct fifty newtons due to slipping. A wet grass condition reduces the total force by twenty percent. The minimum effective push force is five thousand newtons. A stamina drop removes ten percent from the final force. Compute and return a list of adjusted push forces assuming wet conditions and stamina drop. Example input: [(800, 15)], output: [3780.0].

title: Badminton Shuttlecock Drag
spec: Create a simulation using the function `calculate(flights)`. The input is a list of tuples containing initial speed in meters per second and temperature in celsius. The base drag coefficient is zero point four five at twenty degrees. Each degree above twenty decreases the coefficient by zero point zero zero five. The air density at twenty degrees is one point two. The reference area is zero point zero zero two five square meters. The shuttlecock mass is five grams. The minimum drag coefficient is zero point three. Compute the initial deceleration by dividing the drag force by the mass. The force is half the density times speed squared times coefficient times area. Return a list of decelerations. Example input: [(30, 25)], output: [114.75].

title: Table Tennis Spin Trajectory
spec: Build a predictor with the function `predict(shots)`. The input is a list of tuples providing forward velocity in meters per second and topspin rate in revolutions per second. Gravity is nine point eight. The table length is two point seven four meters. The magnus effect downward acceleration is zero point zero one multiplied by the spin rate. The base flight time is the table length divided by the forward velocity. The vertical drop distance is half of gravity times time squared plus half of the magnus acceleration times time squared. An air resistance factor increases flight time by five percent. The net height is zero point one five two five meters. Return a list of tuples with the final drop distance and a boolean indicating if it is a fault meaning the drop is less than the net height. Example input: [(10, 50)], output: [(0.428, False)].

title: Curling Stone Sweeping Friction
spec: Design an evaluator with the entry `evaluate(throws)`. The input is a list of tuples providing initial velocity in meters per second and sweeping intensity as an integer from one to ten. The ice friction base coefficient is zero point zero one five. Each unit of sweeping intensity decreases the coefficient by two percent of its base value. The stone mass is twenty kilograms. Gravity is nine point eight. A debris factor increases the final friction by ten percent regardless of sweeping. Compute the final sliding distance by dividing the squared velocity by two times the final friction coefficient times gravity. Return a list of distances. Example input: [(2.0, 5)], output: [13.73].

title: Yo-yo Sleep Time Calculator
spec: Develop a calculator using the function `compute(throws)`. The input is a list of tuples containing the initial revolutions per minute and a string friction factor as a decimal. The base spin decay rate is fifty revolutions per minute per second. The ball bearing friction adds ten times the friction factor to the decay rate. The minimum throwing speed required to return to the hand is five hundred revolutions per minute. A bearing break in bonus adds five seconds to the final sleep time. The total sleep time is the initial speed minus the minimum speed, divided by the total decay rate, plus the bonus. The maximum theoretical sleep time is one hundred and twenty seconds. The absolute minimum sleep time reported should be zero. Return a list of sleep times. Example input: [(3000, 1.5)], output: [43.46].

title: Juggling Ball Hang Time
spec: Write an analyzer with the function `analyze(patterns)`. The input is a list of tuples containing the peak throw height in meters and the number of props. Gravity is nine point eight. The dwell time in the hand is zero point two seconds per catch. The flight time is two times the square root of two times the height divided by gravity. The total cycle time per ball is the flight time plus the dwell time. The required rate of throws is the number of props divided by the total cycle time. The maximum human throw rate is seven throws per second. A fatigue penalty increases the dwell time by zero point zero five seconds if the props exceed five. Return a list of throw rates. Example input: [(1.5, 5)], output: [3.82].

title: Boomerang Flight Path
spec: Create a model starting with `model(throws)`. The input is a list of tuples containing wind speed in meters per second and launch angle in degrees. The optimal launch angle is forty five degrees. The base return radius is twenty meters. Each degree of deviation from the optimal angle increases the radius by zero point five meters. Wind speed displaces the center of the flight path by two meters per unit of wind speed. The minimum possible radius is ten meters. The maximum catchable offset from the thrower is five meters. A skill bonus reduces the wind displacement by ten percent. Return a list of boolean values indicating if the boomerang remains catchable. Example input: [(1, 40)], output: [True].

title: Origami Paper Folding Thickness
spec: Implement a tool with the function `measure(folds)`. The input is a list of tuples providing the initial paper thickness in millimeters and the target number of folds. The thickness doubles with each fold. A compression loss factor of two percent per fold reduces the new thickness due to paper stretching. A structural failure limit is normally seven folds, but process any number. If the final computed thickness exceeds one hundred millimeters, cap it at one hundred. A density multiplier of zero point eight is applied to the final thickness. A safety trim deducts one millimeter from the final result. The minimum allowed output is the original thickness. Return a list of final thicknesses. Example input: [(0.1, 5)], output: [1.31].

title: Clock Pendulum Tuning
